message.content: 审查一下discord-me这个项目 这个很久之前经过了几轮频繁激进的迭代 可能缺乏很好的历史债的清理和架构审视 并且之前做的一个子功能（orchestration目录下的）需要全部删除 没什么用 设计的反正不是很好 以后要做以后再优化 现在我需要你审查一下所有组件 考虑进行清理和架构优化（梳理一下功能 梳理各个slash command 现在命名也不是很规范 比如fork似乎是new的意思 也可以思考一下是不是改成bun+ts更好一些） 总之以你的历史经验全面的审视这个项目 给出你的优化建议

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- browser-use: Automates browser interactions for web testing, form filling, screenshots, and data extraction. Use when the user needs to navigate websites, interact with web pages, fill forms, take screenshots, or extract information from web pages.
- discord-me: Discord bridges. Three tools — (1) `ask`/`send` — Claude-initiated DM when Claude needs the user AFK. (2) `discord_chat_daemon.py` — user-initiated chat daemon, one persistent session per channel/thread; its `push` subcommand turns a one-shot notification (daily digest, briefing) into a chattable thread the user can reply into. (3) `recap_dm.py` — periodic cross-session recap digest pushed to DM, so multi-channel/multi-thread work stays legible.
- gog: Google Workspace CLI for Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Contacts, Sheets, and Docs.
- native-cli-sessions: Find, list, summarize, and reconstruct native Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, or OpenCode conversations from local session stores. Use for requests about today's Claude chats, recent Codex sessions, this week's Gemini history, local OpenCode transcripts, or reviewing what Codex, Claude, Gemini, or OpenCode was doing on this machine.
- obsidian: Maintain the user's Obsidian vault as a living personal wiki — an interlinked, compounding knowledge base distilled from any source (papers, repos, datasets, photos, conversations, the user's own notes). Use whenever capturing, answering from, or tidying the user's long-term knowledge.
- pet: Local Petty — a persistent companion (default ✨ Claude 星) with personality, mood, drives, and Claude-powered chat. Use when the user wants to check on, talk to, feed, or put the pet to sleep; or when they ask about its state, memories, or to start/stop it.
- pptx-generator: Generate, edit, and read PowerPoint presentations. Create from scratch with PptxGenJS (cover, TOC, content, section divider, summary slides), edit existing PPTX via XML workflows, or extract text with markitdown. Triggers: PPT, PPTX, PowerPoint, presentation, slide, deck, slides.
- voice-notes: Local voice capture pipeline — transcribe audio (including Voice Memos) with Whisper, store raw .srt under ~/.agents/data/voice-notes/raw/, keep a TSV index with category, and query past recordings.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

file.content:
---
name: discord-me
description: Discord bridges. Three tools — (1) `ask`/`send` — Claude-initiated DM when Claude needs the user AFK. (2) `discord_chat_daemon.py` — user-initiated chat daemon, one persistent session per channel/thread; its `push` subcommand turns a one-shot notification (daily digest, briefing) into a chattable thread the user can reply into. (3) `recap_dm.py` — periodic cross-session recap digest pushed to DM, so multi-channel/multi-thread work stays legible.
---

# discord-me

Two independent Discord bridges + a recap loop that glues them together.
Different bots, different purposes.

| | `ask` / `send` (bot1) | `discord_chat_daemon.py` (bot2) |
|---|---|---|
| Initiator | Claude | User |
| Bot | `@<dm bot>` | `@<chat bot>` (separate) |
| Lifetime | One-shot per call | Always-on daemon (launchd) |
| Use for | "I need your input to proceed" | "User pings me from their phone" |

Shared implementation note: both tools connect to the **Discord Gateway
(WSS)** via `discord.py`, so messages arrive push-style in ~100ms instead of
the 3–4s of the old REST-poll design. Scripts declare their deps inline (PEP
723) and are run with `uv run --script`; `uv` materializes a managed venv on
first run and caches it, so there's no manual `pip install`. `uv` must be on
PATH (`~/.local/bin/uv`).

## Routing

Pick the reference that matches the user's intent:

- **First-run / config / launchd install** (any of the three tools, any
  time `~/.agents/data/discord-me/*.json` doesn't exist yet) →
  [references/setup.md](references/setup.md).
- **Claude needs to reach the user** (AFK ping, blocking question, status
  notification) → [references/ask-send.md](references/ask-send.md) covers
  `ask` / `send` / `probe`.
- **User is pinging Claude from Discord** (DM, bound channel, thread,
  `/hook`, `/fork`, slash commands, launchd ops) →
  [references/chat-daemon.md](references/chat-daemon.md) covers the daemon's
  config, operations, slash commands, and troubleshooting. Also covers
  the agent-callable orchestration CLIs (`spawn-run`, `post-message`,
  `stop-run`) and the `/run_*` slash family for observing runs.
- **Designing or editing a multi-agent topology** (yaml schema, message
  routing, `@mention` semantics, finish predicates, run lifecycle) →
  [references/topology.md](references/topology.md).
- **Debugging daemon concurrency, tuning `max_concurrent`, reasoning about
  disconnects / stuck turns / shutdown** →
  [references/chat-daemon-internals.md](references/chat-daemon-internals.md).
- **Adding a new agent / understanding the runner contract** (writing a
  `runners/<name>/runner.sh` script, `--describe` schema, turn invocation,
  output JSON envelope) →
  [references/runner-protocol.md](references/runner-protocol.md).
- **Periodic cross-session recap DM** (digest of all claude sessions pushed
  via bot1) → [references/recap-dm.md](references/recap-dm.md).

## Files in this skill

- `discord_me.py` — bot1 CLI (`ask` / `send` / `probe` / `setup`).
- `discord_chat_daemon.py` — bot2 always-on daemon + `hook` / `unhook` /
  `list` / `push` / `spawn-run` / `post-message` / `stop-run` subcommands. The
  `push` subcommand opens a thread under the configured `feeds_channel_id`,
  posts one-shot content, and drops a seed so the thread's first user reply
  pins an agent (default `opencode`) + flags and gets the pushed content as
  context — that's how daily digests / briefings become chattable. The
  last three drive the orchestration runtime (multi-agent topology
  runs); see [references/topology.md](references/topology.md).
- `topologies/<name>.yaml` — multi-agent run definitions (group,
  reviewer_fix, debate, brainstorm_vote). Bring your own.
- `topologies/finishers/*.py` — optional finish predicates referenced by
  topologies that should auto-close on a condition.
- `orchestration/` — bus, engine, runtime, store, topology loader.
  Daemon imports these; agents and runners do not.
- `harness/` — runner registry + dispatcher; calls runners with the
  same JSON contract whether the turn comes from direct chat or a
  topology participant.
- `discord-chat.plist.template` — launchd template for the daemon
  (`__HOME__`, `__SKILL_DIR__`, `__LABEL__` placeholders).
- `recap_dm.py` — cross-session recap pusher (uses bot1 to send).
- `runners/<name>/runner.sh` — pluggable agent runner scripts. Daemon
  discovers them via `--describe`; add a directory to wire up a new agent.
  See `references/runner-protocol.md`. The bundled `runners/claude/`
  delegates `--describe` from `runner.sh` and execs `runner.py` for turn
  mode (so attachments with images can be sent as `stream-json` blocks);
  `runners/codex/` and `runners/opencode/` are single bash scripts.
  The opencode runner shells out to `opencode run --format json` and
  exposes the local `opencode.json` providers via the `model` flag, plus
  `agent` (build / plan) and `variant` (reasoning effort).

Config lives in `~/.agents/data/discord-me/` (`config.json` for bot1,
`chat_config.json` + `chat_state.json` for bot2, `recap_state.json` for the
recap loop). Tokens grant full bot access — `chmod 600` both config files.
